[[Bureau of Indian Standards|IS 1079]] HR Coils General Engineering steels }} '''Bokaro Steel Plant''' ('''BSL''') is located in the [[Bokaro district]] of [[Jharkhand]]. It is the fourth integrated public sector steel plant in [[India]] built with [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] technology. It is the largest steel plant in India in terms of area (10 km x 5 km). == History == [[File:BSL-SAIL.jpg|thumb|Bokaro Steel Plant gate]] Bokaro Steel project, which is now in Jharkhand after the bifurcation of Bihar in 2000, was planned in the late 1950s. The political elites of Bihar then argued for a case for building a steel plant in Bokaro as Bihar was backwards in terms of industrialisation and the area where the steel plant was proposed was rich in mineral resources required for making steel as it was situated in the Chota Nagpur plateau. The area is rich in coal, iron ore as it is located in Chota Nagpur plateau, which is world famous for rich minerals and mines. The achievement of Self-Sufficiency is a long process, and even as PM Jawaharlal Nehru worked towards that goal, the nation was drawn into closer involvement with the Soviet Union. In September 1964, the Soviets confirmed their readiness to assist in the construction of the huge Bokaro Steel Plant.{{Cite book |url=https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/docs/CIA-RDP85T00875R001100130127-2.pdf |title=Intelligence Memorandum, Indo-Soviet Relations |date=4 December 1972 |publisher=CIA}} The [[Soviet Union]] has traditionally managed to secure generous returns on its aid programme in India.The principal redeeming feature of the preliminary agreement between Bokaro Steel and Gipromez is the Russian commitment that they would see it through to 4 million tonnes ingot capacity, though the phasing and completion dates.{{Cite news |date=17 October 1964 |title=Bokaro, made in the USSR |url=https://www.epw.in/system/files/pdf/1964_16/42/bokaromadeinussr.pdf |access-date=28 July 2024 |work=The Economic Weekly}} [[Heavy Engineering Corporation]] with help of Gipromez developed the [[Bucket-wheel excavator|equipment]] according to Russian specifications.{{cite journal | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4378206 | jstor=4378206 | title=Soviet Collaboration in Indian Steel Industry, 1954-84 | last1=d'Mello | first1=Bernard | journal=Economic and Political Weekly | date=1988 | volume=23 | issue=10 | pages=473–486 }} BSL engineers were trained by the [[Soviet]] engineers, there was also a dedicated Russian colony in Sector 4 of Bokaro Steel City for their stay. The prestigious firm of MN Dastur and Company was actively associated with the early planning of the project and had the competence to assess critically the proposed Soviet designs, however, muscled out by the Soviet negotiators from the final aid contract to the chagrin of an articulate and aroused public opinion cutting across most political parties.{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bqG0AAAAIAAJ | title=The Bokaro Steel Plant: A Study of Soviet Economic Assistance | isbn=9780444103888 | last1=Desai | first1=Padma | date=1972 | publisher=North-Holland Publishing Company }} The steel plant was incorporated as a limited company in 1964.{{cite book|author=Nirmal Sengupta|title=Destitutes and Development: A Study of the Bauri Community in the Bokaro Region|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dQXAoHucmMkC&pg=PA25|year=1979|publisher=Concept Publishing Company|pages=25–|id=GGKEY:73SPC2220UQ}} It was later merged with the state-owned [[Steel Authority of India Limited|Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)]].[http://www.sail.co.in/ Steel Authority Of India Limited] The steel plant started operation in 1972 with Bokaro city construction completed. [[File:Steel Plant, Bokaro Steel City.jpg|thumbnail|right|250px|Bokaro Steel Plant seen from a train]] == Production == Currently, it houses five blast furnaces with a total capacity to produce 5.8 MT of liquid steel.{{cite web |title=BOKARO STEEL PLANT - PRODUCT BASKET |url=https://sail.co.in/bokaro-steel-plant/products}} The plant is undergoing a mass modernisation drive after which its output capacity is expected to be 12 MT. An upgrade of the plant was also done in the 1990s in its steel refining units and continuous casting machines. Initially, about 64 moujas (a mouja may have several village units) had been acquired for the plant. Of the total land acquired, only 7,765 ha was used to set up the steel plant. The rest has been given by SAIL to the private parties without government’s approval. ==Products== Bokaro Steel Plant is designed to produce a wide range of products: # Hot rolled coils # Hot rolled plates # Hot rolled sheets # Cold rolled coils (CRM) # Cold rolled sheets # Tin mill black plates # Galvanised plain and corrugated sheets # Oxygen gas # Hydrogen gas # Coke oven byproducts # Railway tracks # DMR grade # Steel pipes # low weight Stainless steel # Jackal steel # SeQR TMT Bars Bokaro has provided a strong raw material base for a variety of modern engineering industries including automobile, pipe and tube, LPG cylinder, barrel and drum producing industries. ==Financials== Bokaro Steel Plant has achieved a net profit of Rs 600 crore during the financial year 2022-23, which is 45% of SAIL's total profit of Rs 1330 crore.{{cite web | url=https://www.dailypioneer.com/2023/state-editions/bokaro-steel-plant-creates-record-of-production-in-history-of-50-years--amarendu-prakash.html | title=Bokaro Steel Plant creates record of production in history of 50 years: Amarendu Prakash }} ==Collaboration== Bokaro steel plant uses majority of the Blast furnace equipment from [[Heavy Engineering Corporation]], a PSU from Ranchi and some of the equipment's are used from [[Larsen & Toubro]].{{cite journal | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4378206 | jstor=4378206 | title=Soviet Collaboration in Indian Steel Industry, 1954-84 | last1=d'Mello | first1=Bernard | journal=Economic and Political Weekly | year=1988 | volume=23 | issue=10 | pages=473–486 }} ==References== {{reflist}} == Further reading == * {{cite book|author=Sutinder Bhatia|title=Bokaro steel plant: some economic aspects|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=DjUgAAAAIAAJ|date=1 January 1991|publisher=Popular Prakashan|isbn=978-81-7154-540-7}} * {{cite book|author=Padma Desai|title=The Bokaro steel plant: a study of Soviet economic assistance|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ryc0AAAAMAAJ|year=1972|publisher=North-Holland Pub.
